static_traits.name: Chen Jing
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history; no similar planning- and stress-related problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to give specific examples; coherent logic, good cooperation; tends toward self-criticism and uses 'should' phrasing; able to identify and describe emotions and bodily reactions (tension, sleep affected, decreased appetite); neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed and depression due to time-consuming planning and frequent setbacks of moving to another state, attributing delays to one's own 'poor planning ability', causing significant stress and impairing daily functioning (work efficiency, interpersonal relationships, sleep and diet).
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to reduce persistent moving-related stress and overwhelm through counseling, develop healthier coping mechanisms and reduce self-blame.
growth_experiences: At the last art exhibition preparation, facing a pressing deadline, by breaking down tasks, advancing step by step, and seeking friends' help, I ultimately successfully held the exhibition, showing my organizational and collaborative abilities under pressure.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent/I am not capable
I am flawed (unable to handle complex matters)

special_situations.event: When planning to pack the workroom over the weekend, insufficient boxes and more items than anticipated disrupted progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot advance fully as planned and anticipate all needs in advance, it means I am not competent enough, a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Formulates more detailed checklists and stricter deadlines, forcing themselves to execute through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have anticipated needing more boxes; I am not organized enough

special_situations.event: Seeing others' moving processes look smooth on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can complete it easily but I cannot, it proves I am inferior and something is wrong with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with others, trying to plan perfectly, reducing asking friends for help
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone else can handle it, only I cannot

special_situations.event: Whenever setbacks occur during the move (e.g., tasks not completed on schedule)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One setback means my overall ability is poor, and I will keep doing poorly in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles effort but neglects rest, demands more strictly of oneself

special_situations.event: Has friends for support, but has not yet discussed moving challenges with them in detail
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I ask friends for help, I am troubling others and appear incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Bears stress alone, reduces contact with friends to avoid being judged

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and supported, while hoping to maintain competence and a sense of control over life matters
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent or troubling others, being judged and rejected by others
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of self-worth and avoids depending on others through self-blame and redoubled control
Maintains a certain distance to reduce the risk of being evaluated

object_relations.self_representation: Not competent enough, someone needing to bear pressure alone
object_relations.object_representation: Others are more capable people who may judge oneself (or busy people who are hard to support)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When moving plans are disrupted or uncontrollable factors arise (e.g., insufficient materials, excessive tasks)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Generalizing occasional setbacks into 'I am not capable', attributing coping failures to personal flaws (transference: self-deprecation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle, empathic tone; acknowledge their efforts and separate events from self-worth, inviting dissatisfaction toward specific problems rather than the self; use open-ended questioning to help them identify needs and available support.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When Anxiety rises, feeling overwhelmed and trying to regain control through tighter planning
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes that only complete rationalization and strict planning can avoid failure; emotional expression and seeking help would weaken self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First affirm their organizational strategies, then gently guide them to connect bodily sensations (tension, insomnia, decreased appetite) with emotions; help them balance planning and emotion regulation, and gradually tolerate uncertainty.

manifestations: Though having friends to talk to, has not yet discussed moving and planning difficulties in detail, tending to bear pressure alone
In comparing others' narratives of 'smoothly moving house', feels left behind and not a member of the group
outcomes: Sleep and diet affected, bodily tension

manifestations: Feeling uneasy about uncontrollable factors (unplanned setbacks), trying to maintain control with strict planning
Sees failure or deviation as a threat to self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'I should...' self-demands (e.g., I should have anticipated needing more boxes)
Generalizing setbacks into 'I am not capable', excessive self-criticism
Self-denial under others' seemingly smooth narratives, lowering self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Has friends' support but does not seek help in detail, choosing to bear it alone
Turns stress and blame back onto oneself, using self-blame to 'push' behavior rather than seeking external resources

exception_events.target_problem: When moving plans hit setbacks (e.g., insufficient materials, items exceeding anticipation), the client usually blames herself and feels overwhelmed, leading to reduced focus and organization, worse efficiency.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During the last art-exhibition preparation (facing a tight deadline), the client did not fall into self-blame and chaos as usual, but broke tasks down, advanced step by step, and actively sought friends' help, finally completing the exhibition smoothly with good results.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: breaking tasks down and advancing gradually; different support: friends' help reducing load; different understanding: allowing oneself not to be perfect, process-oriented rather than harshly result-judging.

positive_force: Has the ability to break down tasks and steadily advance them under stressful situations (experience preparing art exhibitions)
Having a mobilizable network of friend support
Able to identify and willing to challenge negative thought patterns (e.g., overgeneralization, personalization)
Willing to try new methods and conduct behavioral experiments, holds a certain sense of hope
negative_force: Excessive self-criticism and self-blame, often constrains oneself with 'should' rules
Unwilling to ask friends for help in detail, resources not yet effectively utilized
Sleep and diet affected, bodily tension intensifying stress
Cognitive biases (overgeneralization, personalization) amplify the impact of setbacks

target_behavior.behavior: Self-blame and negative self-evaluation when moving plans are blocked, with Anxiety and bodily tension
antecedent: Setbacks in the moving process (e.g., insufficient materials, excessive tasks)
Plans not yet completed on schedule, time exceeding anticipation
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic interpretation and overgeneralization of setbacks, personalized cognition, attributing specific problems to overall incompetence, maintaining control through self-blame.
target_behavior.function: Escaping Anxiety from uncertainty, and gaining temporary control and motivation through self-punishment.
target_behavior.consequence: Increasing stress, declining focus and organization, affecting sleep and diet, interpersonal tension, lower overall efficiency.

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids asking friends for detailed help and communicating; tends to bear it alone
antecedent: Feeling overwhelmed or worrying about being judged by others
Self-worth decreases after seeing others' social media presentations of 'moving house smoothly'
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing appearing incompetent or troubling others, worrying about being evaluated and rejected.
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential rejection or negative evaluation, maintaining the safety boundary of self-image.
target_behavior.consequence: Support network not yet fully utilized, loneliness and increased stress, further tension in Interpersonal relationships, impaired moving efficiency.
